## Natural history notes

A medium-sized bumble bee characterized by its fuzzy black body, yellow thorax, and mostly black abdomen with a pale yellow first abdominal segment. In Florida, it is found in gardens, farms, fields, forest edges, parks, roadsides, and other open or semi-open habitats with abundant flowering plants, especially in northern and central parts of the state. Adults visit many flowers for nectar and pollen and are important pollinators of wildflowers and crops, while colonies nest in abandoned rodent burrows, grass tussocks, compost piles, or other sheltered cavities near or below ground.
